correctness.rationale: Exact conditional tree coupling shows moving the parent of arrival j changes total path length by S_{j,n} times the depth change, and E S_{j,n}=n/j independently of all earlier choices. This gives the individual contribution n(H_{i-1}+1-H_{j-1})/[j(j-1)], and telescoping proves the exact total. The partial-sum increments have one sign change and its infinite limit is strictly negative by inverse-square integral comparison. Harmonic and inverse-square expansions prove the 2 i^2 log i threshold. A standalone checker independently enumerated all recursive trees through n=9 and confirmed 120 exact-analytic and numerical threshold assertions; finite computations are corroboration, not infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The candidate is the exact covariance of one specified nonroot birth-label outdegree with all-node total path length and a unique positive-to-negative sign transition at the sharp horizon n~2i^2 log i. Prior published and indexed root-attachment theorems provide only label one; known joint degree/depth laws for finitely many marked vertices do not cover sum of depths of all vertices or the sign threshold. Targeted searches and material inspections found no equivalent or stronger claim; implicit broader-framework derivability remains an explicitly identified risk.
residual_risks: The root-specific covariance proof suggests a general parent-reparenting technique; unlocated literature could apply that technique to all labels.
Finite-vertex marked degree/depth results might imply related global moments after a nontrivial growing-dimensional summation.
Some broader increasing-tree generating-function analyses might encode the exact covariance without displaying the sharp unique-threshold theorem.

value.rationale: For a labeled nonroot vertex, the very same local outdegree measure switches from positive to negative dependence on total root search cost as the time horizon grows; the root has only the negative regime.
